title: MOFA thanks Formosa Club for again holding annual conference in Taiwan
text:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung sincerely welcomes parliamentarians from various European nations who traveled to Taiwan to attend the annual conference of the Formosa Club in Europe. Held in Taipei for the first time in 2025, the annual conference is being held in the city again this year.

From October 24 to 28, 49 parliamentarians from the European Parliament and the parliaments of 19 European nations are attending the annual conference and related activities. The opening ceremony on October 24 coincided with a typhoon, yet the parliamentarians persisted in making the journey to Taiwan despite the inclement weather. Minister Lin expresses his sincere appreciation for the staunch friendship they demonstrated to Taiwan.

In his remarks at the opening ceremony, Minister Lin thanked the Formosa Club for having consistently served as a vital bridge connecting Taiwan with its democratic partners across Europe and for firmly supporting Taiwan’s international participation as well as peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait since its 2019 founding. He stated that Taiwan was continuing to strengthen cooperation with Europe in such spheres as economics, values, and alliances under the framework of integrated diplomacy, expressing his hope that these efforts would lead to the joint establishment of trusted non-red supply chains for AI, drones, and other critical technologies. Minister Lin added that in the face of China’s transnational repression through its enactment of the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, Taiwan would continue to enhance cooperation with like-minded partners in Europe to jointly safeguard its hard-earned democracy and free way of life.

Chair of the European Taiwan Friendship Group and Cochair of the Formosa Club Michael Gahler, who was serving as chairman of the annual conference, remarked that the heavy rain and wind were a reminder that while no one could control the weather, everyone could control how to respond. He continued by saying that the international situation was as unpredictable as the weather. He stressed that as Russia and China were engaging in authoritarian expansionism through various means, like-minded partners needed to formulate responsive policies to prepare for any possible scenario. Mr. Gahler urged relevant parties to remember that the presence of parliamentarians from various European nations in Taiwan was a demonstration of such determination. He expressed hope that, building on parliamentary friendships linking Taiwan and Europe, participants would continue to steadily advance Taiwan-Europe relations.

At the conference, the parliamentarians adopted a joint statement friendly to Taiwan, demonstrating through concrete action that there is staunch support for Taiwan in other countries’ parliaments. The statement reaffirmed a steadfast commitment to deepening interparliamentary cooperation between Taiwan and Europe. It endorsed the establishment of trusted and resilient supply chains in AI, drones and unmanned systems, advanced semiconductors, and other critical technologies. The statement also backed Taiwan’s RISK Management Initiative on International Undersea Cables, which was put forth by Minister Lin at the Taiwan-Europe Undersea Cable Security Forum in 2025.

The statement expressed serious concern over China’s Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress and recognized the resolutions adopted by the European Parliament in April and October this year condemning the law’s extraterritorial provisions as a form of transnational repression. Moreover, the joint statement strongly opposed any practice that would unilaterally alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait, reiterated that United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758 did not determine Taiwan’s status, and supported Taiwan’s meaningful participation in international organizations and mechanisms.

At a dinner on the day of the opening ceremony with members of the Formosa Club, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs François Chihchung Wu once again thanked the parliamentarians for having journeyed to Taiwan despite the typhoon. He said that their willingness to travel under such difficult circumstances highlighted their firm friendship with Taiwan.

MOFA hopes to continue to strengthen Taiwan’s friendships and cooperation with the European Parliament, national parliaments, and democratic partners through the annual conference, the Trusted Technology Forum for Democracies, receptions, and other related activities to collectively safeguard freedom, democracy, and the rules-based international order. (E)
